purpose: Part of the next-100 candidate titles content-flag backfill, resume group 3 of 4, live CSM research.

contentFlagModel.mappingNote: This refetch preserves CSM's current visible category label and proposes the nearest app level. Production catalog edits should be made only by the follow-up importer/reviewer.

entries.title: Akeelah and the Bee

violence.summary: Two girls bully Akeelah for being a "brainiac" and push and shove her before the principal intervenes.

language.summary: Infrequent profanity and put-downs including "s--t," "ass," "hell," "damn," "freak," "idiot," and "turd juggler."

romance.summary: Middle schoolers kiss each other on the cheek.

drinking.summary: A positive character smokes a cigarette and another drinks a whiskey on the rocks but doesn't act drunk.

handoffNotes: Brief conversations reference the death of family members -- a father killed in neighborhood gun violence and a daughter lost to disease -- which may warrant gentle prose context for sensitive readers.

entries.title: Au Revoir, les Enfants

violence.summary: Gestapo searches, a circumcision-check scene, and sustained psychological tension dominate rather than overt on-screen brutality.

language.summary: Schoolboys use occasional profanity including "bastard," "s--t," and the ethnic slur "yids"; a sign reads "No Jews Allowed."

romance.summary: Only subtle references to adolescent curiosity about masturbation and girls.

drinking.summary: Schoolboys of various ages sneak cigarettes and smoke in several scenes.

handoffNotes: This is a profoundly sad WWII story about a Catholic school hiding Jewish boys under Nazi occupation; the ending involves the boys and a priest being taken away by the Gestapo, an implicit deportation/death that will need gentle, age-appropriate prose context for younger readers.

entries.title: Hugo

violence.summary: Hugo's father dies in a fire, the station inspector's dog is set on unaccompanied children who are jailed and threatened with the orphanage, and Hugo has nightmares involving a train and transformation.

language.summary: Mild insults include "idiot," "no-good thief," "liar," and "drunk."

romance.summary: Adults flirt and hold hands, married characters embrace and kiss, and Hugo and Isabelle hold hands with a cheek kiss; humorous adult talk references marriage and infidelity.

drinking.summary: Uncle Claude drinks from a flask and is obviously drunk, and wine glasses appear at the train station cafe.

handoffNotes: Hugo's father dies in a fire early in the story and Hugo is orphaned, a grief/loss theme that may need gentle prose context for younger readers.

violence.summary: Teen wrestling and fighting, an implied cow shooting, bullying, and implied assault injuries.

language.summary: Insults and obscenity substitutes such as "idiot," "frickin'," "retarded," "crap," "sicko," and "flippin'."

romance.summary: Mild kissing and embracing plus comical marketing of an herbal breast-enhancement product; no nudity.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern for this title.

violence.summary: Pratfalls, nightmares, cartoonish chases, underwater wrestling, a gun display without injuries, a casualty-free car crash, and potentially frightening clowns, devils, dinosaurs, and the character Large Marge.

language.summary: One instance of "crap," the phrase "burn in hell" in a music video, and Pee-Wee's trademark "I know you are, but what am I?"

romance.summary: Mild flirtation and romantic tension, plus a kissing scene within a movie-within-the-movie.

drinking.summary: A scene set in a biker bar, and Pee-Wee dances to a song.

entries.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark

violence.summary: Frequent peril and hand-to-hand battles with guns, a frightening face-melting climax, vengeful-ghost imagery, and encounters with poisonous snakes and large spiders; a man is killed when his head hits a plane propeller.

language.summary: One instance of strong profanity plus "goddamn," "hell," "bastard," and "damn."

romance.summary: Kissing and flirting, with implied sex between Indy and Marion -- he's shown shirtless getting out of bed.

drinking.summary: A character wins a drinking contest by consuming large quantities of alcohol.

handoffNotes: CSM notes the film is insensitive toward people of color, who are depicted as violent, uneducated, and barbaric -- worth flagging for parents even though it isn't one of the 4 scored flags.

entries.title: Romeo and Juliet

violence.summary: Bitter quarreling leads to murder and suicide, with some deadly swordplay.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful language concern.

romance.summary: A nude male posterior and a glimpse of breasts appear in a tasteful bed scene.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: The story ends in the deaths of both title characters (murder and suicide); CSM specifically warns that teens may perceive the narrative as romanticizing suicide, which warrants parental discussion and gentle prose context.

entries.title: Rudy

violence.summary: A fiery plant explosion kills Rudy's best friend, and full-contact football practice scenes show bleeding wounds and bruises.

language.summary: Profanity includes "Bullsh--t," "ass," "crap," "goddamn," and "pissed off"; a coach threatens to "beat the s--t out of" tryout candidates.

romance.summary: Rudy approaches college women to introduce to his shy tutor in exchange for tutoring help.

drinking.summary: Rudy becomes intoxicated at a bar and reveals information that gets him removed from the booster squad; additional bar scenes appear.

handoffNotes: Rudy's best friend is killed in a fiery plant explosion partway through the film, a sudden-loss/grief moment that may need gentle prose context.

entries.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse

violence.summary: Intense large-scale action, destruction, and explosions with close-up fighting, frequent suspense/peril, and mortal danger; a Peter Parker/Spider-Man and an important secondary character both die during the film.

language.summary: "Crap," "hell," "dang," "freakin'" plus insults like "janky," "broke," "fat," "stupid," "dumb," and "pig."

romance.summary: Miles flirts with Gwen and they make eyes at each other but go no further than hugging; dialogue references having "game."

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: A version of Peter Parker/Spider-Man dies early in the film and an important secondary character also dies later, real grief/loss beats that may need gentle prose context for younger readers.

entries.title: Time Bandits

violence.summary: Considerable cartoonish violence including an arm ripped off in arm wrestling, battle explosions, knights speared dead on javelins, the Titanic crashing, people on fire, and scary pursuing figures like a floating face.

language.summary: References to "hell," "damn," "shut up," plus name-calling and some problematic slurs.

romance.summary: A brief nude painting, showgirl costumes, minimal innuendo, and flirting couples.

drinking.summary: Characters drink alcohol frequently without appearing intoxicated, cigars are smoked once, and one scene involves injected sleeping drugs.

handoffNotes: Suicidal ideation is played for laughs in one scene, and Kevin's parents ignore or berate him throughout -- both may warrant gentle prose context for sensitive readers even though the film itself has no character death/grief arc.

entries.title: West Side Story

violence.summary: A big fight scene leads to two characters being stabbed to death, and the film also features a sexual assault and a fatal shooting.

language.summary: Profanity and derogatory ethnic slurs including "spic" and "Polack."

romance.summary: A brief reference to sex work and some kissing.

drinking.summary: A musical number references drug use and characters smoke cigarettes.

handoffNotes: The Romeo-and-Juliet-inspired plot ends with two characters stabbed to death in a gang fight, a significant grief/loss theme that may need gentle prose context for younger readers.

entries.title: The Witches

violence.summary: Scary witches and children in peril, including a baby in a carriage pushed down a hill (rescued), and Luke's parents killed in an offscreen accident.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful language concern.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: Luke's parents are killed offscreen early in the story, and CSM specifically flags that children may be upset both by that death and by Luke's seeming indifference to it -- this needs gentle prose context.

language.summary: Mild language appears in song lyrics, including a reference to "shake your booty."

romance.summary: Flirtation and an almost-kiss between the leads, one cheek kiss, and a shirtless scene in a changing room.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: CSM's live age rating (8+) is one step above the current catalog value (7+); minor discrepancy worth a light review.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

entries.title: You Lucky Dog

violence.summary: Guns appear (mostly tranquilizer darts) with no serious injuries, booby traps cause characters to trip and fall, a death is shown in flashback, and dangerous driving is depicted.

language.summary: Occasional curses and derogatory terms such as "heck," "moron," "numskull," "fruitcake," "maniac," and "lowlife."

romance.summary: A character is shown bathing with partial nudity from the waist up.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: The plot hinges on a millionaire's recent death (his dog inherits the fortune) and that death is shown in flashback -- may need gentle prose context for younger readers.

language.summary: Mild profanity including "butt," "jerk," "wuss," plus one instance of racist language directed at a Peruvian character.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

entries.title: Smart House

violence.summary: A character is bullied with visible injuries (black eye, bruising); the smart home delivers electric shocks to bullies, shows a menacing skull hologram, imprisons residents, and electrifies door handles; historical footage of Nazi rallies and atomic explosions also appears.

language.summary: Mild language, usually in a bullying context, including "geek," "kick-butt," "dead meat," and "shut up."

romance.summary: References to attraction between characters; an adult couple kisses and a teenage girl kisses a boy on the cheek.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful drinking, drug, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: The story is built around the death of the protagonist's mother before the film begins, and the smart house is explicitly used as an attempted maternal replacement; the film also addresses his father moving on to a new relationship -- this grief and family-loss thread may need gentle prose context.
